question_text: Why are incinerators used in hospitals?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.62, VSAQ 164). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Hospital waste
lines: Hospitals produce hazardous waste such as

steps.why: The question asks why, so the answer must start with the problem: the waste is hazardous, and that is the reason an ordinary bin will not do.
common_mistakes: Writing only that hospitals produce a lot of waste. It is the HAZARDOUS kind that matters.
Starting with the incinerator. The reason comes first, the device second.
steps.memory_tip: Answer a why question in two halves: the problem first, then the device that solves it.
steps.margin_note: Name two or three kinds of waste, then say it must be treated.

steps.label: What the incinerator does
lines: An incinerator burns the waste at a high
microorganisms and reduces the waste to ash.

steps.why: Burning is only half the answer; the mark is for what the burning achieves — the microorganisms are destroyed — because that is what makes the waste safe.
common_mistakes: Writing that the incinerator stores the waste. It BURNS it.
Leaving out the microorganisms. Destroying them is the point of the high temperature.
steps.memory_tip: High heat does two jobs: it kills the microorganisms and it cuts the waste down to ash.
steps.margin_note: One line on the burning, one on what the heat destroys, one on the result.

insider_note: This is a why question, so an answer that only describes an incinerator scores half — say what the waste is and what the heat destroys.
